*One brand system for everything, generated into every consumer and gated in CI.*

> **Never write a brand value into a file by hand.**

## Why install this

PRESS is the warm-paper editorial brand shared by a morning brief, a city
profile, a budget report, a résumé, a LinkedIn card, a dev-log cover, every
generated workflow masthead, and natejswenson.com.

Before this skill it existed as **eight hand-ported copies across four
repositories**, with five different names for the same orange, three genuinely
shared token groups declared nowhere at all, and no way to notice when one copy
moved. That is not a discipline problem — it is what happens to any value that
can be copied.

`brand/tokens.json` is now the only place a brand value is written down.
Everything else is generated from it into a **marked region** inside an otherwise
hand-written file:

```python
# >>> press:tokens v0.9.0 sha256:2b3d… GENERATED by @natjswenson/press, do not edit
DEFAULT_THEME: dict = { ... }
def load_theme() -> dict: ...
# <<< press:tokens
```

The consumer keeps everything else — its 250-line stylesheet, its poster
geometry, its personal avatar footer. Whole-file generation clobbered
ghostwriter's avatar footer once already, which is why regions exist.
`press check` re-derives each region and fails CI on any difference.

## What you get

| Path | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `skills/press/brand/tokens.json` | **The** source of truth: colours, font stacks, identity, limits. |
| `skills/press/brand/laws.md` | The accent law, structure, the three voices, the tracking ceiling. |
| `skills/press/brand/components.md` | The shared vocabulary: masthead, standfirst, big stat, ledger, duel, terminal. |
| `skills/press/brand/agent-ui.md` | How a skill's run should read in the chat transcript. |
| `skills/press/brand/voice-core.md` | The copy rules that hold for every artifact. |
| `skills/press/targets.json` | Every place the brand is written down. |
| `skills/press/bin/press.js` | The CLI: `check`, `emit`, `lint`, `doctor`, `propagate`, `tokens`. |

## Quick start

```bash
npx -y @natjswenson/press@latest check --repo .     # is this repo in sync?
npx -y @natjswenson/press@latest emit  --repo .     # make it so
npx -y @natjswenson/press@latest lint theme.css     # mechanical brand law
npx -y @natjswenson/press@latest doctor             # the whole registry
npx -y @natjswenson/press@latest tokens --format css
```

**Always pin a version or `@latest`.** A bare `npx @natjswenson/press` silently
prefers a stale global install over the registry — the failure that cost this
repo a release with a sibling skill.

## Triggers

- "the PRESS look"
- "check the brand is in sync"
- "why do my colors differ"
- Composing or restyling any artifact — a report, résumé, card, cover, PDF, HTML
  page or chart.
- Adding a skill that renders anything, or changing a brand value everywhere at
  once.

## Requirements

- Node 18+, no dependencies.
- Nothing else. Every command is offline; `propagate` is the only one that talks
  to a network, and only when pointed at another checkout.

## What `check` fails on

| Status | Means |
|---|---|
| `drift` | the region exists but its bytes differ |
| `missing` | the file has no region — the generated block was deleted |
| `absent` | a declared file is not there |
| *(empty run)* | **zero targets resolved — the check verified nothing** |

The last two matter most. A checker that verifies nothing reports "all clean",
which is exactly how a gate turns decorative.

## Integrity is not freshness

Two different questions, and conflating them is what leaves a consumer silently
stale:

| | Question | Answered by |
|---|---|---|
| **Integrity** | does this region match the press version this repo adopted? | `press check`, against a **pinned** version |
| **Freshness** | has this repo adopted the **current** brand? | `press propagate`, pushed from here |

A pinned check passes forever against the version it was pinned to. This skill's
own site consumer sat two releases behind with entirely green CI.

## What it does not own

Layout and composition (the medium's business), chart colour validation (the
`dataviz` skill), and any voice learned from the user's own writing —
ghostwriter's learned profile and devlog's release-note shape stay where they are
and win on conflict. PRESS sets the floor everything shares, not the whole of
anything.

## Adding a consumer

Declare it in `targets.json`, choose an emitter (`python-theme`, `python-consts`,
`css-vars`, `md-palette`, `markdown-block`, `readme-masthead`, `gha-header`,
`json`), give it an `init` anchor naming the hand-written block the region takes
over, then:

```bash
npx -y @natjswenson/press@latest emit --target <id> --init
```

Aliases are deliberate: the résumé keeps `--sig`, the site keeps `--fg`. The
names stay idiomatic to their medium; only the values are shared.

## Development

```bash
cd skills/press/skills/press
npm test
```

Node skill. `ci / press` runs the same tests plus `press check` over every target
whenever press *or any file it writes into* changes, and each consumer's own
`ci / <skill>` job re-checks just its region — so drift fails in the pull request
that causes it.
